newsitem.title: USA: Rouge Steel approves capital projects.
newsitem.headline: Rouge Steel approves capital projects.

text.p: Rouge Steel Co said Friday that its board of directors approved two new capital projects worth a total of $72 million and named a new director to fill a vacant board seat.

Rouge Steel said it will spend $31 million on a new raw material handling system to support its iron-making operations, which includes a new stock house, charging system and reclaiming system for the company's blast furnaces. Construction on the project, which is expected to reduce costs and boost productivity, is expected to commence in November and be completed in September 1997.

Rouge Steel also said its board approved a $41 million expenditure for the company's share of previously-announced joint venture projects with Worthington Industries Inc to construct and operate a cold-rolled, hot-dipped galvanizing plant in Frenchtown Charter Township, Mich.
The new facility is expected to produce approximately 450,000 tons per year of galvanized and galvanneal products, primarily for automotive applications, Rouge Steel said.

Construction is expected to start in January 1997, with completion targeted for mid-1998. Upon completion, Rouge Steel said the joint venture plant will allow the company to process a larger portion of its steel into higher margin, value-added products.

In a separate action, Rouge Steel said its board appointed Shiloh Industries Inc Chairman Dominick Fanello as a Rouge Steel director for the remainder of the term vacated by Pete Klisares, who resigned on August 1.
